D005-D015_h001.question:
I’ve been working at the café for about a year now, but lately, it’s been hard just to get out of bed and show up. For the past six months, I’ve felt completely drained—like there’s no point to anything. I don’t enjoy my favorite music anymore, I can barely eat, and I’ve lost so much weight my coworkers have noticed. Some days, I cry before my shift and pretend I’m fine.

The weird part started about two months ago. I began smelling this burnt odor, like something’s always on fire—even when no one else smells it. At first, I thought it was the espresso machine, but it followed me home. Then, I started believing I wasn’t just a barista. I became convinced I’m actually a prophet, chosen to deliver a message that’ll change the world. I feel this power inside me, like I’m connected to something divine.

But here’s the thing—when I was doing a little better last winter, none of this happened. The voices, the smell, the belief in my special purpose—they only came when I was at my lowest. I don’t feel powerful. I just feel broken.
D005-D015_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h001.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling completely overwhelmed for the past six months—just constant sadness, like a heaviness I can’t shake. I don’t enjoy anything anymore, not even working with my patients, which used to be so rewarding. I’m exhausted all the time, sleep too much, and can barely concentrate—even simple tasks feel impossible.  

About two months ago, things got worse. I started tasting something awful—like metal or rot—in everything I eat, even water. My husband says there’s nothing wrong, but I *know* it’s there. I’ve also become convinced someone’s watching me, maybe even poisoning my food. I’ve checked the locks five times a night. At first, I thought it was stress, but it hasn’t gone away.  

The thoughts and tastes only started *after* I sank into this deep depression—I didn’t have them before, and they don’t happen when I’m not depressed. I’m scared, but I also feel numb, like I’m failing my family and my job. This all hit around the same time my mood crashed—nothing like this ever happened in my life before.
D005-D015_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h002.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h003.question:

And my mind tells me I’m not just a real estate agent—I’m meant to save people through divine knowledge. I keep thinking I can predict who will buy a home before they even walk in, like I’m chosen for something bigger. 

But these visions and thoughts? They only come when I’m at my lowest. When I feel slightly better, they fade. They’ve never been there without the crushing sadness. It’s like the darkness brings the delusions with it.

D005-D015_h015.question:
